lastMessage:
Pushed successfully (99dc738). orb/knowledge.json remains untouched (unrelated background dashboard file).

Summary

1. Idle baseline restored: lcp-measured-results.json was holding a deliberately-loaded run for five archetypes â€” sandbagged data that would show fake improvement against any future measurement. Moved loaded-run data to lcp-load-experiment.json and 15-trial data to lcp-trials-experiment.json; re-measured idle fresh (the original idle run's raw data had already been lost to an overwrite) and restored it as canonical.

2. The px/byte mechanism didn't replicate â€” retracted. A second idle-vs-loaded test showed ASSEMBLE and FLYTHROUGH drifting similarly (not the dramatic 12%-vs-2.4% split from round 1). Built real decomposition instead: transfer time is load-independent for every archetype (â‰¤1.7%), decode time isn't (+10% to +96%). Both "outliers" turned out to be transfer-dominated, not decode-dominated â€” meaning the previously-proposed "second heavy control" fix would have targeted the wrong axis, exactly as you suspected.

3. TRANSFORM headroom measured, not guessed: WebP quality 0.6 and frame count 16 each recover real time with no/minor visible cost; resolution reduction was rejected outright (real, guaranteed upscale blur on desktop, contradicting this project's own prior finding). The quality+frame-count combination clears 2.5s by ~1.4-1.5s â€” about 7x the largest noise figure measured anywhere in this investigation â€” with the grain texture confirmed preserved by both std and screenshot. Recommended, not applied â€” it's a real product change to the shipped archetype, so it's queued as a sign-off task rather than silently shipped.

Vault and TASKS.md updated, committed (99dc738), pushed. No spending, external accounts, or scope changes involved.
